transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello there, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I, um... I guess I came in because I've been noticing a few foolish habits I've picked up, and I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing about them. I just keep steering clear of my own workshop out back. And... well, I've also been avoiding any family get-togethers if there's a chance my brother-in-law might be there. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly for a man my age to act like that, but after all this time, I'm just getting tired of planning my whole life around making sure I don't run into those reminders. I hope I'm explaining that right for you... is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things more often than not, even when there isn’t a specific reason to be?

Well, no, Doctor, I wouldn't say that. I hope that's alright to say. I don't really sit around fretting over nothing. I've always tried to be a pretty steady fellow, you know? 

It's really just... well, just those specific things I mentioned before that get me worked up. Otherwise, I'm right as rain, really. I try not to make a fuss if there's no good reason for it. I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers here... did that make sense?
Do you ever feel uneasy or anxious about being in places or situations where it might be hard for you to leave quickly or where you feel trapped?

No, no, I wouldn't say I feel trapped or anything like that. I mean, I go to the grocery store, I go to church... I'm perfectly fine in crowds or, you know, waiting in line. I don't get all panicky about not being able to leave. 

I really try to just go about my business like anyone else. I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking about? I don't want to give you the wrong impression, I'm really quite comfortable in most everyday situations. Is that helpful?
When you're faced with those specific situations—like being in your workshop or being around your brother-in-law—do you feel a sudden rush of intense anxiety or panic?

Well, no, not a sudden rush, Doctor. I wouldn't call it panic, exactly. I don't want you to think I'm losing my head or anything like that. 

It's more just... a strong discomfort, I suppose? Like I'd just really rather be anywhere else, so I just steer clear before it even gets to that point. I don't go having fits or anything dramatic. I hope that's alright to say... I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. Does that sound like what you were asking?
Doctor: When you avoid your workshop or family gatherings, is it because you’re worried that you might have a panic attack or experience intense anxiety in those places?

Well, goodness no, Doctor. I wouldn't say I'm worried about having a... a panic attack, or anything dramatic like that. I'm not sitting around afraid I'm going to lose my head or make a scene. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm being difficult, but it's really not like that at all. 

I just prefer to stay away because, well, it just brings up things I'd rather not think about. It's more about just keeping my peace of mind, you know? Just quietly keeping to myself so I don't get bothered by it all. I'm certainly not scared of having a fit. 

I hope that's an alright answer to give... I just want to be sure I'm explaining myself properly so I don't waste your time. Am I making sense?
Can you tell me a bit more about what specifically in the workshop or about your brother-in-law makes you want to avoid those situations?

Well, it's... it's a bit embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I don't want you to think I'm dwelling on things or... or losing my grip. But sometimes, just out of nowhere, I'll... I'll see his hand. With that heavy tool. 

It's like a picture that just pops right into my head when I'm not even trying to think about it. I could just be shaving, or working on a little painting, and there it is. And I have to admit, it still makes my chest tighten up a bit when it happens. 

I hope that doesn't sound too strange, Doctor. I really try to just push it out of my mind and keep busy. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Doctor: When you see that image of your brother-in-law's hand with the tool, does it feel like you're reliving a past event, or is it more like just remembering something unpleasant?

Well, it's... it's really just a memory, Doctor. I wouldn't say I'm reliving it, no. That sounds a bit... well, a bit extreme, doesn't it? Like I'm losing touch with reality or something. I assure you, I know exactly where I am and what year it is when it happens. 

It's just an unpleasant memory that flashes by, like remembering a bad fall or... or dropping a nice piece of china. It's just a quick picture, and then I shake my head and go back to what I was doing. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I really am doing quite well otherwise. 

I hope it's okay to put it that way. I just want to be sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how I'm handling things. Does that make sense?
Since you mentioned seeing that image of your brother-in-law's hand, do you find yourself feeling angry, fearful, or upset when those memories come up?

Oh, goodness no, I wouldn't say I get angry. I try very hard not to be a bitter sort of person, Doctor. I really don't hold any grudges, it's just not in my nature. 

And as for being fearful or upset... well, maybe I feel just a tiny bit startled for a split second, sort of like when a door slams unexpectedly? But I certainly don't get all worked up or emotional about it. I'm not sitting around crying or shaking my fist, I promise you that. 

I just take a quiet breath and go right back to my crossword or my painting. I try to keep a pleasant attitude, you know, so I'm not a bother to anyone around me. I hope it's alright that I don't get angry about it... I just think it's better to let sleeping dogs lie and not make a fuss. Am I doing the right thing by just brushing it off like that?
Doctor: Do you find that you’re less interested in things you used to enjoy, or that you don’t feel pleasure in activities the way you used to?

Oh, no, Doctor, I wouldn't say that at all. I still very much enjoy my little routines. Like I mentioned before, my painting and my crosswords... they still bring me quite a bit of joy, really. 

I think it's so important to keep busy, don't you? I certainly wouldn't want to just sit around the house moping all day—I imagine that would be quite a burden on the people around me, and I really try my best not to be a bother to anyone. So, yes, I still find plenty of pleasure in my day-to-day activities. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things to keep my spirits up and stay active.
Doctor: Do you ever find yourself feeling down, sad, or hopeless for most of the day, more days than not, even if just a little bit?

Oh, no, Doctor. No, I really don't. I mean... sure, everyone has a quiet afternoon here and there, but feeling sad or hopeless? No, I wouldn't say that at all. 

I try very hard to look on the bright side of things. I count my blessings, you know? I think it's just so important to keep a cheerful disposition. Nobody likes a sourpuss, and I'd just hate to bring down the mood for my family or the neighbors. I always try to put on a smile and make the best of things. 

So, no, I'm generally quite content with my days. I hope that's the right way to go about it? Just staying positive and not dwelling on gloomy things... that's healthy, isn't it?
Doctor: Do you ever feel emotionally numb or detached from people, activities, or parts of your life that used to mean something to you?

Oh, heavens no. Numb? No, I really don't think so. I care very deeply for my family and my friends. I try to be as warm and present as I possibly can be. I'd just feel terrible if anyone ever thought I was giving them the cold shoulder or pulling away from them. That just wouldn't be polite at all. 

I still feel very connected to the folks in my life and the things I do every day. I make it a point to check in on people and really listen, you know? I think it's so important to stay engaged and show people you care, don't you agree? I certainly wouldn't want to become one of those cold, distant types... I hope it's okay that I still feel so attached to everything? I just try to be a good, supportive person to have around.
When you see that image of your brother-in-law's hand, do you ever feel guilt, shame, or a sense that something bad is your fault?

Well, I... I suppose I do feel a little bit of guilt sometimes, yes. I try not to dwell on it, of course, because I know it doesn't do anyone any good to wallow. But... when that image pops into my head, I... I just keep telling myself I should have put my foot down sooner. 

I should have never let him stay with us in the first place. I just think... maybe none of this would have happened if I'd handled it like a man, you know? If I'd just been a bit firmer. I didn't want to cause a fuss at the time, I just wanted to be accommodating... but now I feel like I let everyone down by not speaking up. 

I know I shouldn't beat myself up over it, and I really do try to focus on moving forward. It's just hard not to feel a little responsible sometimes. I hope you don't think poorly of me for feeling that way? I know I should have been stronger, but I'm really trying my best to make things right now.
Since this memory of your brother-in-law's hand with the tool comes up, do you find yourself avoiding thinking about it or trying not to feel any emotions connected to it?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I avoid it. I mean, I certainly don't try to shut off my feelings or anything like that. That wouldn't be very healthy, would it? 

I just... well, if the thought pops up, I try to acknowledge it and then just gently move on to something more productive. I don't want to sit around brooding over it, because I know my wife needs me to be steady. I just try to keep myself busy with chores around the house or reading a good book. 

I'm not running away from it, I promise. I just prefer to focus on the positive things in front of me instead of getting all tangled up in bad memories. That's the right way to handle these things, isn't it? Just keeping a stiff upper lip and carrying on?
Have you noticed any other memories or thoughts related to that event coming up unexpectedly, or is it mainly just the image of the hand with the tool?

Well, no, not really. It's... it's mostly just that one image of his hand. I don't really have a lot of other thoughts or memories popping up like that. I try to keep my mind on other things, you know? 

I mean, sometimes I might think about the situation in general, just wishing I had handled things differently, like I mentioned. But as far as sudden memories catching me off guard... no, it's really just that one specific picture in my head. 

I hope that's alright? I don't want to make it sound like I'm hiding anything from you. I just... I really don't have a whole lot of other memories intruding on my day. That's a good sign, isn't it? It means I'm doing okay, mostly?
Since this memory first came up, have you noticed any lasting feelings of anger, fear, or sadness connected to it, or do you feel mostly neutral about it once you move on?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say there's any anger. Or fear, really. I mean, maybe just a brief sigh about the whole mess when it happens, but once I move on to my chores or my reading, I feel... well, mostly neutral, just like you said. 

I really try my hardest not to let things fester. Holding onto sadness or getting angry, well, that just sours a person, doesn't it? I wouldn't want to put my wife through that. I like to think I'm pretty level-headed about it all once the moment passes. I just want to keep things peaceful at home, so I just let it go. 

That's the best way to be, don't you agree? Just staying calm and not making a mountain out of a molehill? I hope I'm handling it the right way.
Since this memory first came up, have you noticed any persistent feelings of guilt or shame, or do you feel mostly at peace with it once you move on?

Oh, guilt? Or shame? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I certainly don't sit around feeling ashamed of myself or anything like that. That wouldn't do anyone any good, would it?

I mean, sure, sometimes I think about how I could have... well, maybe smoothed things over better back then. But it's not a heavy guilt or anything that weighs me down. Once I get back to my book or fixing something around the house, I feel perfectly fine. At peace, just like you said. 

I try to be a good husband, a good man. I don't let myself get bogged down in those kinds of negative feelings. It's better to just look forward, right? I'm doing the right thing by just staying positive and moving on, aren't I?
Since this memory first came up, have you found yourself going out of your way to avoid anything that reminds you of that event, beyond just the workshop and your brother-in-law?

Well, no, not really anything beyond that. I mean, the workshop and, you know, family gatherings where he might be... that's really the main thing. I suppose that's actually the whole reason I finally decided to come in and talk to you. 

I just... I realized I've been spending so much energy just steering clear of my own tools, my own space. And then trying to figure out if he's going to be at a birthday or a holiday dinner before I say we'll go... it's just getting a bit tiresome, you know? Planning my whole schedule around not running into him or those reminders. 

But I haven't been avoiding anything else! I still go to the hardware store, I still see the rest of the family. It's just those two specific things. That's not too unusual, is it? Just wanting to keep the peace and avoid an awkward situation? I think anyone would do the same, wouldn't they?
Since this memory first came up, have you noticed any lasting negative beliefs about yourself, such as 'I am to blame' or 'I can't handle things,' even if just occasionally?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I think I can't handle things. I mean, I've managed my household for years, right? I'm a capable man. 

But... well, I suppose sometimes, just occasionally, I do catch myself thinking that maybe... maybe I should have just put my foot down sooner. You know, when he first asked to stay with us. I keep telling myself that if I had just said no right from the start, if I had handled it more like a man and protected our home... well, maybe none of this would have happened. 

I don't dwell on it! I really don't. It's just a passing thought now and then. It's normal to look back and wonder if you could have done things a little differently, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm being honest with you, but I don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself. That's just a normal way to look at a mistake, right?
